claims.text: Researchers remain unclear about important aspects of Natural Language Generation (NLG) evaluation.
Current classifications of hallucination and omission in data-text NLG can be synthesized using a logic-based approach.

evidence.description: The author notes that despite advances in NLG and LLMs, researchers are still unclear about important aspects of NLG evaluation.
The author examines current classifications of hallucination and omission in data-text NLG to propose a logic-based synthesis.

methodologies.name: Logic-based synthesis
methodologies.description: A logic-based synthesis of existing classifications of hallucination and omission in data-text NLG.

limitations.text: All current thinking about hallucination has remaining limitations.
